consolidation_breakout.description: A second way in, for when AAVE never comes back down to its average: buy the break out of a quiet band.
consolidation_breakout.condition: The 24 bars before the current one sit inside a band no wider than 2% (highest high / lowest low - 1). The first bar to close above that band's top is the break; 60 minutes later the 1-minute close must still be above the top, and the buy lands on the next minute's open. Only the first break of each quiet stretch counts.
consolidation_breakout.market_filter: Only the blocked hours are shared with the dip rule. The downtrend filter is deliberately NOT applied: requiring the averages to be stacked upward before a break screens out exactly the breaks that start a new trend.

exit.note: A break comes out of a quiet band rather than a dip, so it carries its own tighter stop and its own trail.

trailing_stop.note: The arm was raised from +1.276% to +1.75% in September 2026. It applies to DIP lots only - a Mode C lot keeps its own +1.283% arm, where the later arm was measured to do nothing.

portfolio.sizing_rule: Every coin that is switched on shares one pot of equal lots, set in the dashboard. A trade buys one full lot when a lot is free and the wallet has the USDT for it; when less than a full lot is left, the buy uses what is left. Money is never set per coin.

provenance.backtest_bnb_fees: Oct 2024 - Sep 2026 with 3 equal lots; percentages are of the starting money. With the earlier +1.276% arm: +38.6% over 289 trades (255 dip, 34 breakout) at an 85.1% win rate, max drawdown -7.88%, five of six walk-forward windows. With the +1.75% arm now deployed, the same period gives +38.8% over 271 trades at 79.3%, walk-forward +41.2% against +34.7%, better in six of six windows, at a -10.23% mark-to-market drawdown. The breakout alone: 38 trades, +8.1%, an 89.5% win rate, six of six windows and a -1.36% drawdown.
provenance.caveats: A trend exit was tested and deliberately left out. On paper it added about +33% of the money, but a walk-forward selection test put its honest contribution at +0.7%: the gain came from a few large moves in the first year and the right line length could not have been chosen in advance (16h +56%, 24h +69%, 36h +41% - a spike, not a plateau). AAVE wins small and often, which is what the giveback trailing stop is for. The quiet-band breakout, by contrast, improved four of six windows at every setting tested.
provenance.arm_change: Sept 2026 recheck: every other deployed setting was confirmed, but the dip's trail armed too early. Walk-forward rises steadily with the arming level (as % of the money) - +1.276% arm +34.7%, +1.5% +37.2%, +1.75% +41.2%, +2% +47.1%, +2.25% +54.9%, +2.5% +59.0% - and inside a pre-committed range of no more than double the deployed arm, choosing honestly beat leaving it alone (+42.0% against +34.7%), the only setting change in the whole research programme to pass that gate. +1.75% was chosen as the conservative point: better in 6 of 6 walk-forward windows (+0.39, +0.09, +0.09, +0.83, +1.32, +3.75 = +6.5 points of the money) at a -10.23% mark-to-market drawdown against -9.62%. The cost is win rate: 85.2% -> 79.3%, fewer and larger wins. The gain is entirely in the dip lots (+33.6% -> +40.3% over the full window); the breakout is unaffected and its own arm was left alone. An ATR-scaled arm reaches the same place (0.4x ATR = about +2.9%) and adds nothing over a fixed number, so the fixed number is used.
